prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up to outbound load control handoff; airline loading excluded. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor, alias Tern (sets congestion thresholds, confirms overload response, authorizes recovery, notified of isolated bags, reviews flights moved earlier and directs priority, may defer lower-priority bags). Security Duty Manager (alarm decisions). Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (security holds; produces Custody Seal Log). Maintenance Technician (isolates failed section, confirms route safe). Airline Ramp Coordinator (accepts staged bags; sends Carousel Release Slip; reports loading-readiness changes). Induction: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (Oversize Exception Ticket); Bag Tag Printer (Calibration Witness Tag); Transfer Bag Feeder (Late Transfer Bag Card); Induction Tray Conveyor (admits by priority, scan confirmation, safe spacing). Interlocks stop feed on jam/open door/downstream not ready. Control: Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (tag-flight link; validates sort plan vs schedule; applies cutoff profiles per carrier/flight/condition; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; compares remaining time with route estimates; alternate route only if screening/timing valid; diverts bad bags to Secondary Inspection Chute; keeps recoverable association while disposition pending). Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (induction permissive, matches demand to capacity; Recovery Route Card). Flight Data Gateway, alias Lantern (flight data, revisions, dispatch targets; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory). Screening: North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel, and South Gate Scanner (record outcomes; Manual Rescan Receipt); Image Resolution Desk; Bag Reconciliation Station (Bag Match Query). Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (routes by assignment and cutoff priority; Chute Occupancy Note). Make-up: East/West Make-Up Conveyors; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit, alias Orchard (presents only after grouping and screening confirmed); Outbound Load Control Desk (uses planned dispatch and load-close targets). Requirements: hold bad-data bags; induct only with valid record/route/ready equipment; incomplete exams never cleared; routing withheld until image disposition; threat suspends routing until security disposition; unscreened bags held from final induction; cutoffs include screening/sort/make-up/transfer allowances; accepted bag keeps flight unless change requires reassessment; missed-cutoff bags held for reassignment; make-up allocation starts when assignment and build positions confirmed.

New part:
S132: Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes release to a make-up position only when the flight remains within its processing window.
S133: Flight Data Gateway maintains the flight identity and departure timing used for make-up planning.
S134: Mosslight assigns bags to active make-up lanes using current zone status.
S135: Velvet records each bag's screening disposition and release state against its flight assignment.
S136: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages accepted bags for onward processing without changing their flight association.
S137: Induction Tray Conveyor meters bags into the handling stream at a rate that avoids accumulation at the make-up interface.
S138: Primary Crossbelt Sorter separates bags according to their authorized destination and current operating status.
S139: North Gate Scanner verifies readable bag identification before bags proceed toward their assigned build.
S140: South Gate Scanner provides the corresponding verification for bags processed in its coverage area.
S141: Image Resolution Desk uses the exception ticket to confirm an authorized make-up position for an oversize bag.
S142: Secondary Inspection Chute retains bags requiring further examination until the applicable disposition is recorded.
S143: Bag Reconciliation Station uses the Late Transfer Bag Card to reconcile a transfer bag against its intended flight.
S144: Transfer Bag Feeder meters accepted transfer bags into the active handling sequence without bypassing required checks.
S145: East Make-Up Conveyor delivers assigned bags to the designated make-up position at a controlled rate.
S146: West Make-Up Conveyor provides the equivalent delivery function for positions in its operating area.
S147: Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit maintains bag order and position information for its active flight build.
S148: Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit receives the Carousel Release Slip only after its position and flight assignment have been checked.
S149: Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms staffing, equipment availability, and the planned loading sequence before accepting a build for loading.
S150: Outbound Load Control Desk reconciles the completed build against the permitted flight load before departure closeout.
S151: Bag Tag Printer produces replacement identification only when authorized personnel have confirmed the required bag details.
S152: Security Duty Manager resolves release holds that require a security decision before bags can enter a departure build.
S153: Maintenance Technician reports equipment restrictions that affect lane availability or safe bag delivery.
S154: Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates changes to build priority with airline ground operations and communicates any resulting delivery constraints.
S155: Manual resolution begins when an image or identity exception prevents automatic processing from establishing a reliable disposition.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
